details:
Hello! I am developing a custom locomotion application and found a serious bug regarding how VRChat handles Head-Relative movement via OSC when physical controllers are put away.

The Issue: When using OSC (/input/Vertical and /input/Horizontal) for movement, the movement correctly follows the "Head Directed" locomotion setting only when physical VR controllers are active. However, as soon as you put the controllers down and VRChat switches to Hand Tracking mode, the OSC movement breaks: it stops following the HMD orientation and becomes Absolute (World Space). Moving "forward" via OSC will permanently move you North in the world, regardless of where you look.

Why this is definitely a bug: If you reproduce the exact same scenario but use a physical Xbox Controller instead of OSC, the Xbox joystick correctly moves you relative to your Head orientation even while in Hand Tracking mode. The system logic correctly handles the Xbox controller, but fails to apply the same relative coordinate transform to the OSC input.

Expected Behavior: OSC /input/Vertical should respect the "Head Directed" locomotion setting and behave exactly like an Xbox Controller joystick while Hand Tracking is active.

Steps to Reproduce:

Enable OSC in VRChat.

Set Options > Locomotion to "Head Directed".

Put down your physical VR controllers to activate Hand Tracking.

Push forward on an Xbox Controller -> You move relative to where you look (Correct).

Send /input/Vertical 1.0 via OSC -> You move along the absolute World Z-axis, ignoring your head rotation (Bug).

This severely limits hands-free accessibility tools and leg-tracking locomotion utilities. Thank you for looking into this!
title: BUG: OSC Locomotion (/input/Vertical) loses Head-Relative orientation and becomes World-Absolute during Hand Tracking
